chapter: Minton's, Louis Armstrong and the South
title: Joining Louis Armstrong: "Little Gizzard is modern"
summary: Around 1940-41 he left Minton's for Louis Armstrong, who defended him against manager Joe Glaser; the band included Joe Garland, Prince Robinson and Luis Russell.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: In what, did we say, '41.
'41. Yeah, because see I was there quite a few times. The first time --
Because listen --
I went to Minton's, I guess it must have
been around 1940.
Yeah, I think so too. That's what I was going to say.
Yeah. But then I left and went with Louis Armstrong.
Well, tell me how come.
You know, because I was always trying -- looking for something bigger and better to do.
You were trying to climb the ladder.
Yeah, which Louis understood, because when Joe Glazer wanted to fire me because he said my name wasn't big enough, so Louis said, 'Leave Little Gizzard there. He's modern.'
Louis said that.

Now, that's when I figured what I was doing was right, no matter what anyone thought. When Louis says -- he called me Little Gizzard -- he said, 'Little Gizzard is modern,' and that did it. Now I knew right away. So when I left the band he gave me a picture and cried and his tears were on the picture.
Well, doesn't that say a wonderful lot for Louis, too?
Oh, Louis was the first modern musician.
Yes.
So therefore he could understand, you
know, when he -- when he heard something that was akin to what he had been doing all his life, he recognized it immediately. So the guys in the band, we had, oh, like Prince Robinson and --
Oh, that was the big band?
Yeah. All the old cats, you know. Well, Joe Garland, he was the musical director. Had Prince Robinson, and what was this other --
Had Luis Russell on piano.
Luis Russell on piano, and what's this saxophone player?
Oh, Cole?
That's right. That's right. What was his first name? Rupert.
Rupert.
Rupert Cole.
His son is a drummer.
Oh, yeah?
Ronnie.
Oh, I didn't know that.
Yeah, I think so.
George Washington, trombone player.
Yeah. They were kind of an ancient band.
Yeah. And so --
